newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat falls again, seen at critical point.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat falls again, seen at critical point.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures continued to fall on Thursday and brokers said the market had reached a critical point where it could move either way.

Sydney's fall was despite local tight supply and a large reduction in the 1997/98 crop forecast, although it was in trend with fund selling in the U.S., Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd told Reuters.
Market leader January 1998 sold down A$1.00 a tonne to A$170.00 on the previous settlement close, with 10 lots traded.
Settlement prices across the board were down by A$1.00.
Opinions on the market were sharply divided, Booth said.

Market bull points were strong demand and forecast El Nino drought in Australia. Ord Minnett also believed that world supply would surprise on the lower side, while demand would surprise on the upper side.
Market weakness, however, was based on fund selling and farmer hedging in the U.S., as well as on memories of last year's strong market decline at this time of year.
Signs were "quite ominous" that the U.S. could move into a downtrend, he said.
Good news, further hedging and fund selling could take the bottom out of the market. In this case it could fall significantly, he said.
But the market was very over-sold and Ord Minnett believed its downside was restricted, he said.
